hypothesis: Portfolio equity-curve adaptive sizing (anti-Martingale): when trailing equity is in drawdown >5% below its 20-day high-water mark, scale new entry notional to 0.7x. This is a portfolio-level risk allocation overlay that reduces exposure during adverse equity-curve regimes without changing entry/exit signals.

novelty.new_evidence_axis: portfolio-level trailing equity high-water mark sizing is a new mechanism distinct from per-signal risk multipliers and static notional scalars

prediction.confidence_reason: The system max drawdown is 11.19% in mid_weak with 52% win rate suggesting clustered losses. Anti-Martingale sizing is theoretically sound (Kelly criterion implies sizing proportional to edge). No prior experiment has tested portfolio-level equity-curve-responsive sizing; nearest neighbor exp-20260524-002 was per-signal heat haircut, a different mechanism. Main risk: only 18-22 trades per window means sizing changes affect very few entries, and 5% DD threshold may trigger too late or not at all in the shallow-drawdown windows.
